title: Chapter 5.  Polity & Governance - Current Structure & Leadership

blocks.content: Building on the constitutional framework of Chapter 4, this chapter covers Delhi's present-day governmental structure, current officeholders, and the judiciary - all frequently tested current-affairs facts that change with each election/appointment cycle, so verify close to your exam date.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Governance structure focuses on the distinct powers of the Executive, Legislature, and Judiciary.
The Executive and Legislature are responsible for policy formulation and lawmaking.
The Judiciary maintains constitutional oversight and resolves legal disputes.
Parliamentary Representation forms the basis of democratic governance and civic participation.

cells: Lieutenant Governor, appointed by the President of India
Shri Taranjit Singh Sandhu (former diplomat/Ambassador to the US), in office since 11 March 2026, succeeding Vinai Kumar Saxena (who moved to become LG of Ladakh)
Chief Minister, appointed by the LG based on ability to command confidence of the Assembly
Smt. Rekha Gupta (BJP), 9th CM of Delhi and its 4th woman CM, in office since 20 February 2025
70 seats; BJP 48, AAP 22 (post-2025 Assembly election) - the first BJP majority government in Delhi since 1998
Smt. Atishi Marlena (AAP), herself a former Chief Minister (2024-25)

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Rekha Gupta's February 2025 victory ended AAP's decade-long (2015-2025) hold on Delhi government - a major current-affairs turning point. Track the CM sequence: Sheila Dikshit (INC, 1998-2013) -> Arvind Kejriwal (AAP, 2013 briefly, then 2015-2024) -> Atishi Marlena (AAP, 2024-25) -> Rekha Gupta (BJP, 2025-present).

items: Delhi has its own dedicated High Court - the Delhi High Court - established in 1966, exercising jurisdiction over the entire NCT (unlike some smaller UTs that share a neighbouring state's High Court).

Below the High Court, Delhi's district judiciary is organised into multiple District Courts corresponding to its revenue districts, alongside specialised tribunals and fast-track courts for specific categories of cases.

cells: All 7 seats won by the BJP in the 2024 general election - the third consecutive Lok Sabha election (2014, 2019, 2024) in which BJP has swept all 7 Delhi seats
Members elected by the Delhi Legislative Assembly under proportional representation

items: Questions frequently test constitutional provisions related to Executive and Legislative roles.
Leadership roles and organizational structures within the Judiciary are regularly featured in polity sections.

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: A notable current-affairs pattern: Delhi has voted very differently at the national/Lok Sabha level (consistently BJP since 2014) versus the Assembly/local level (AAP-dominated 2015-2025, BJP from 2025) for most of the past decade - a 'split-ticket voting' phenomenon frequently discussed in Indian political-science commentary.

items: Current LG (2026): Taranjit Singh Sandhu, since 11 March 2026.
Current CM (2026): Rekha Gupta (BJP), since 20 Feb 2025 - 9th CM of Delhi, 4th woman CM; Deputy CM Parvesh Sahib Singh Verma.
70-seat Assembly: BJP 48, AAP 22 (2025 election) - BJP's first Delhi Assembly majority since 1998.
7 Lok Sabha seats, all BJP (swept in 2014, 2019 and 2024); 3 Rajya Sabha seats.
Delhi has its own dedicated High Court (est. 1966) - unlike UTs that share a neighbouring state's High Court.
